title: Model Metadata Schema v1 - draft notes (field brainstorm + rollout edge cases)
content:
Working notes for schema v1. This is intentionally messy / early. Goal is to capture: (1) field list candidates, (2) what Console/Rollouts needs, (3) how changelog generation will consume the fields, and (4) gaps + open questions.

---

0) Problem statement (why we’re doing this)
- Customers are seeing behavior changes without a clear model/version identifier they can trust.
- Today we have: docs pages, slack announcements, and occasional runtime release notes, but no single canonical record.
- Console rollouts need to reference “what changed” at the moment the rollout was executed (esp for regulated customers).
- Support needs to answer: “what version did we serve?”, “when did it change?”, “can I rollback?” quickly.

Non-goal reminder (v1): auto-generated narrative about quality changes from eval diffs. We can link to evals + include a few headline metrics but we’re not going to have the system write a full story yet.

---

1) Primary entities (current thinking)
- model_id: stable ID for a logical model family in Redwood catalog (e.g., “redwood/llama3.1-70b-instruct”).
- version_id: immutable ID for a specific served artifact/config. Needs to be unique globally (NOT just within model_id).
- deployment / availability is a separate concept from model/version identity:
  - hosted availability (region, tier)
  - dedicated availability (customer-specific capacity)
  - private availability (customer-specific installs)

We keep mixing these concepts in conversation; schema should force separation.

---

2) Draft field list (schema v1)

2.1 Identity + naming
- model_id (required)
- version_id (required)
- display_name (customer-facing, optional but strongly recommended)
- description_short (customer-facing)
- description_long (customer-facing, optional)
- aliases (list) (ex: legacy names; internal routing names?)

Notes:
- Need a naming convention doc for model_id: lowercase, slashes, hyphens, no spaces.
- version_id: should be opaque-ish but readable? e.g., “2026-02-12” is tempting but doesn’t encode hotfixes well.

2.2 Provenance / source
- provider (enum: meta, mistral, google, redwood-finetune, etc.)
- upstream_model_name (string)
- upstream_version / revision / commit (string)
- weights_source (enum: upstream, customer-provided (private only), redwood-derived)
- license (string)
- release_date (date)
- training_cutoff (date-ish string; often not exact)

Customer visibility: some of this is sensitive depending on contracts (esp if we have custom variants). May need internal fields + public allowlist.

2.3 Artifact + runtime config (the “what is actually being served” bit)
- architecture_family (llama, mixtral, qwen, etc.)
- parameter_count (string; sometimes “70B”)
- context_window_tokens (int)
- tokenizer (string)
- modalities_supported (text, image?, audio?) (v1 probably just text)
- quantization:
  - quantization_type (bf16/fp16/int8/int4/etc.)
  - quantization_recipe_id (internal reference?)
- serving_engine (ex: redwood-runtime) + engine_version
- kernel_profile / attention_optimization (internal-ish)

Open question: how much of the runtime config is “model metadata” vs “serving metadata”? For changelog purposes, customers care about any config change that can change outputs or perf.

2.4 API surface compatibility (what breaks customers)
- openai_compat_level (string or enum)
- supports_streaming (bool)
- supports_tools (bool)
- supports_function_calling (bool) (may collapse into supports_tools)
- supports_structured_output (bool)
- supports_json_mode (bool)
- max_output_tokens (int) (or derived from context)
- stop_sequences_supported (bool)
- logprobs_supported (bool)
- seed_determinism_notes (string) (customers ask why seed doesn’t guarantee exact match)

Notes from Console/Rollouts:
- Rollouts UI wants a simple “compatibility flags” panel and an explicit “breaking change?” badge.

2.5 Safety / policy notes (customer-safe)
- safety_policy_version (string)
- disallowed_content_handling (string; very careful wording)
- pii_handling_notes (string)
- jailbreak_resistance_notes (string)

Concern from Docs: we should avoid claims that are hard to prove (“jailbreak-proof”). Prefer: “updated safety policy enforcement; see policy doc” + link.

2.6 Performance + cost metadata (mostly for selection + release notes)
- baseline_latency_ms (p50/p95?) (but these are deployment-dependent)
- throughput_tokens_per_sec (again depends)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_estimate (hosted only; again depends)

Idea: store relative performance deltas when they’re meaningful (e.g., “~12% lower p95 latency for 8k prompts on H100”) rather than absolute values. But we need a place to hang that data.

2.7 Availability / lifecycle
- status (active | deprecated | retired | preview)
- availability_tiers (hosted: standard/premium?)
- regions (for hosted)
- effective_date (when version becomes default / visible)
- sunset_date (for deprecated)
- replacement_model_id / replacement_version_id

2.8 Deprecation + migration messaging
- deprecation_reason (enum-ish)
- customer_messaging (string; must be customer-safe)
- migration_guide_url
- rollback_supported (bool)
- rollback_window_days (int)

Support note: customers need clear timelines and whether pinning will continue to work after sunset.

2.9 Links
- changelog_url (computed/published output)
- eval_report_url(s)
- benchmark_dashboard_url
- docs_url

2.10 Audit/editorial
- schema_version (v1)
- created_by, created_at
- last_modified_by, last_modified_at
- change_event_id(s) (ties to changelog generator)
- review_state (draft | in_review | published) (this might live on “changelog entry” not on model/version record)

RBAC reminder: not everyone should be allowed to edit all fields.

---

3) Console + Rollouts edge cases to design for

3.1 A/B tests across model versions
- Rollout A/B means: same model_id, multiple version_id live simultaneously.
- Need to represent “default routing policy” separately from model version metadata.
- Console needs to show: “You requested model_id X; resolved to version_id Y; rollout policy at time of request was Z.”

3.2 Pinned version vs moving default
- Customer pins model_id + version_id (or pins “channel”?)
- If pinned, we must guarantee no silent updates.
- BUT: we may still do runtime-level changes that affect outputs/perf without changing model artifact (kernel changes, batching changes). How do we represent that?
  - Suggestion: model changelog entries can include “runtime impact” sections when runtime release affects that model/version.
  - Alternative: separate “runtime changelog” feed; Console cross-links.

3.3 Hotfixes
- Sometimes we need to hotfix an issue quickly (tokenizer bug, safety config misapplied) without wanting a big public announcement.
- Product stance from Marissa/Paula: hotfixes still need a changelog entry, but we can keep it short and factual.
- Need to prevent “same-day multiple edits collapse” (Michael flagged this as a generator hazard).

3.4 Region-specific rollouts
- Hosted can roll out new version in us-east first, then eu-west.
- Should changelog be global or per-region?
  - For v1: global entry with “availability” section that can indicate region gating.
  - Console should show per-account “effective availability” anyway.

3.5 Dedicated vs Hosted differences
- Dedicated customers may have custom kernel/batching settings; perf numbers won’t match hosted.
- Dedicated customers also ask “did anything change in our environment?” separate from “model version changed”.
  - We likely need per-deployment “serving config” changelog in the future.

3.6 Private deployment / on-prem constraints
- Private can’t depend on public docs site always.
- Need an exportable artifact (signed JSON) that can be stored on customer side.
- Private customer may want a separate approval flow; but v1 can reuse the same workflow with different publish targets.

---

4) Notes from stakeholder interviews (high level)

4.1 Product (Marissa Cole)
- Wants a consistent taxonomy for customer-visible notes: “New model”, “Update”, “Deprecation”, “Compatibility”, “Performance”, “Safety policy update”.
- Wants release note entries to always answer:
  - What changed?
  - Who is impacted?
  - What do I need to do (if anything)?
  - Can I rollback/pin?
- Strong preference: avoid “internal vendor names / nicknames” in public output.

4.2 Rollouts (Paula Mendes)
- Rollouts page needs to link to the exact changelog entry that was published at the time of the rollout.
- Wants “breaking change” to be machine-readable so Rollouts can warn before executing.
- Wants a clear way to state: “This update changes defaults only; pinned versions unaffected.”

4.3 Release engineering (Connor O’Brien)
- Needs alignment with freeze windows:
  - during RC/freeze, only emergency changes can be published
  - generator should support “draft now, publish later”
- Needs a deterministic ordering for multiple events + an immutable history.

4.4 Docs (Elliot Price)
- Wants a strict style template and a linter so we don’t ship weird language.
- Wants consistent section headers for scanning and translation later.
- Very sensitive about the distinction between “policy change” vs “model capability change”.

4.5 Support readiness (Dev Patel)
- Needs an internal-only section in the workflow (not public) that includes:
  - known issues, regression signatures
  - suggested mitigation prompts
  - escalation owner / oncall
- Wants “customer safe summary” to avoid over-claiming. Also wants the ability to quickly correct confusing wording with audit preserved.

---

5) Public vs internal fields (redaction / allowlist)
- We should maintain an explicit allowlist of fields that are eligible to be rendered publicly.
- Everything else is internal-only by default.

Potential internal-only candidates (tentative):
- exact kernel flags / batching thresholds
- vendor/partner contract identifiers
- internal nicknames
- raw evaluation prompts (depending on IP)
- incident references

Open question: do we support “public summary overrides” where PM/Docs can rewrite the summary without changing underlying metadata? Might be necessary.

---

6) Unresolved questions / decisions needed

6.1 version_id format
- Option A: semantic-ish: vYYYYMMDD.N
- Option B: content-addressed / hash-based
- Option C: provider revision + Redwood suffix

Criteria:
- Must be immutable and unique.
- Must be safe to expose to customers.
- Must work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

6.2 What constitutes a “version” change vs “metadata update”?
- If we change only descriptions/links, should that emit a public changelog entry?
  - Maybe separate “customer-visible fields changed” from “metadata housekeeping”.

6.3 Performance metrics representation
- Do we store perf metrics per hardware class? per region? (likely too much for v1)
- Could store links to dashboards instead and a human-written headline.

6.4 Safety/policy updates
- Some policy changes affect outputs without model weights changing.
- We need a consistent way to represent “policy version changed” as a first-class changelog category.

6.5 Evals links + access control
- If eval report is in internal tooling, we should publish a customer-safe view or at least a summary.
- For enterprise, might need a “customer portal” link.

6.6 Backfill strategy for old models
- We won’t have full historical notes pre-migration.
- Support wants a canned line: “Historical entries prior to <date> may be incomplete.”

---

7) Next steps (action items)
- Quentin: write a concrete proposal for required vs optional fields for v1 (by end of week).
- Chloe/Jada: validate what the Console needs as “must-have” in MVP; specifically breaking change flags + compatibility panel.
- Michael: list which fields can realistically be backfilled for top 50 models, and which will be “unknown” initially.
- Elliot: provide initial customer-safe template headings (impact/compat/deprecation/links).
- Connor: confirm what we need for freeze windows + emergency publish path.

---

Appendix: quick examples (very rough)

Example: model_id = redwood/llama3.1-70b-instruct
- version_id: ???
- context_window_tokens: 8192
- quantization_type: bf16
- supports_tools: true
- status: active
- deprecation: none

Example: deprecation entry (fields we need)
- status: deprecated
- sunset_date: 2026-06-30
- replacement_model_id: redwood/llama3.2-70b-instruct
- customer_messaging: “This version will be retired on 2026-06-30. Please migrate to …”

(Need to ensure migration messaging is consistent and doesn’t promise identical outputs.)
